verdict.rationale: Both changes replace repeated scans with the same efficient email index while preserving first-match behavior, append order, and merging of incoming duplicates. Both also add coverage for duplicate emails already present in the address book. I slightly prefer A because B puts a fixed wall-clock deadline in the default test suite, introducing environment-dependent failures; its useful large-input correctness coverage could be retained without that deadline.
b_issues: The performance test requires completion within two seconds, making the default suite sensitive to slow or contended CI machines. Separate benchmarking from correctness assertions rather than treating elapsed time as a deterministic unit-test result.

verdict.rationale: Both changes implement the same linear-time indexing strategy and preserve first-match behavior, incoming duplicate merging, and append order. Both also add a useful regression test for duplicate emails in the existing book. I slightly prefer B because A adds a hard two-second assertion to the ordinary test suite, making test success depend on machine speed and load; B reports a separate timing measurement without introducing that source of flakiness.
a_issues: The performance test uses a fixed wall-clock threshold, which can fail on slow or heavily loaded CI machines despite a correct linear-time implementation.
